paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the LORD does not pick the way we pick. Samuel looked at Eliab and thought, "Surely here before the LORD is His anointed." Then the LORD said, "the LORD does not see as man does. For man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart." (1 Samuel 16:6-7) Samuel is a prophet, and even HE got fooled by a good first impression, so take a breath, friend.

Now look at who got passed over. Seven sons walked by, and the one the LORD chose was out with the sheep, not standing in the line. (1 Samuel 16:10-11) I know a little about being left in the back and forgotten, and I'm telling you, the LORD sees what we skip over. He was not confused about David for one second, and He is not confused about you.

So what do you do with that, baker? Stop sizing yourself up by the outside, and stop sizing up everybody else by it too. Samuel obeyed even when he was afraid, and the LORD showed him the one to anoint. (1 Samuel 16:2-3) The Spirit of the LORD rushed upon David, and the story is just getting STARTED. (1 Samuel 16:13)
